LESSON: CELL STRUCTURE AND SPECIALIZATION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: BIOLOGY
Strand: Cell Biology and Biodiversity
Topic 1.3: Cell Structure and Specialization
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 30

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Cell Structure and Specialization, part of Cell Biology and Biodiversity in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 BIOLOGY.

Key inquiry question: Why do plant and animal cells differ? 2. How are cells specialized?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Cell Structure and Specialization together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner cooperates and shares information in groups as they use

photomicrographs to compare the structure of plant and animal cells as seen under electron microscope.

• Digital Literacy: The learner gains digital literacy while searching for information on structural and functional

differences between light and electron microscope.

Values:
• Respect: The learner demonstrates tolerance, respecting peers during the group discussion on the use of

photomicrographs to compare the structure of plant and animal cells as seen under electron microscope.

17

• Responsibility: The learner searches for information from appropriate internet sites on the structural and functional

differences between light and electron microscope.

18

Scalpels/wide handled scalpels, cover slips, pair of forceps, adjustable tables, biology course books, iodine solution,

ruler/ handled ruler, microscope/adapted microscopes, microscope slides, droppers, laboratory technician, learner

support assistant, photomicrographs of specialized plant and animal cells,
